indicator_definition: The employment rate is the proportion of persons aged 20 to 64 who are in employment, expressed as a percentage of the total population in that age group. It is one of the most widely used indicators of labour market performance. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS).
rationale: A high employment rate is central to economic prosperity, social inclusion and the sustainability of social protection systems. Increasing employment requires policies supporting job creation, skills development and removing barriers to participation. Progress means a sustained increase in the employment rate.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Employment follows ILO standards: persons who worked at least one hour for pay or profit during the reference week. Data are published annually and quarterly by Eurostat.
